notes: Page title: Compléments sur transformation de Coxeter d’un système de racines, with the circled irreducibility insertion and (Kostant). No date, authorial page number, or explicit page count is visible. The bottom-left 1 is archive foliation only.

The page states an eigenvalue-order assertion attributed to Kostant, then a centralizer/normalizer corollary, a proof using a regular eigenline, a criterion for regular eigenvectors, and the beginning of another corollary.

The margin asks Quelle extension de (Z/hZ]* par Z/hZ obtient-on ?. This is a question in the source. The left note asks for an exchange with cor. 3; its final verbal ending is uncertain, and no terminal question mark was seen.

The proof says il faut prouver que son noyau est réduit à 1 and then gives an argument. Reste à prouver ... c^n est conjugué de c is followed by ce qui résulte également de Kostant. These are source proof transitions, not a declaration that a step remains unverified.
The conjugacy formula visibly uses c^h although n is quantified in that sentence and c^n occurs later. The algebraic issue prompted attention to the tall h ascender; no emendation was made.

Overprinted est, en, un and Bn|On have no securely separable earlier whole word or established layering order. Their visible composite readings remain marked rather than inventing hidden canceled tokens.
The three bottom layers are all retained: upper canceled Considérons, baseline canceled Soit D une, and live raised Soit D une. The final s of régulières is actual ink.
The physical last word fragment is élé- at the right edge. The transcript retains the C join convention élé followed by a comment, so the line-division hyphen is not treated as a lexical hyphen.

The first dimension insertion keeps its internal stagger in TikZ and a comment records its left-margin position and open-circle call. The right-margin question is also laid out in TikZ, including the displaced par.

math_checks.check: Conjugacy consequence with the printed exponent h
math_checks.performed: Using the stated order h of c, c^h=1. Thus wcw^{-1}=c^h would imply wcw^{-1}=1 and hence c=1 after multiplication by w^{-1} and w. For nontrivial c this conflicts with the intended conjugacy assertion.
math_checks.limit: This elementary internal consistency check does not determine the printed exponent; the visible h is retained. No external theorem checked.

math_checks.check: Last inference of the necessity paragraph
math_checks.performed: If c has order h and c^{h\prime}=1, then h divides h\prime. Combined with 0<h\prime≤h, this gives h\prime=h.
math_checks.limit: Checked only this order-divisibility inference, assuming the regular-stabilizer assertion used by the text; that assertion and Kostant’s results were not proved.
